title: Routine Check-Up
correct_orders: Imaging studies (X-ray, CT, MRI as necessary)

rationale.Complete Blood Count (CBC): To evaluate the patient's overall health and detect potential issues with red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets.
rationale.Chemistry Panel: To assess kidney function, liver function, electrolyte levels, and glucose levels.
rationale.Urinalysis: To evaluate kidney function, detect urinary tract infections or other abnormalities.
rationale.Electrocardiogram (ECG): To evaluate the patient's heart rhythm and cardiac health.
rationale.Imaging studies (X-ray, CT, MRI as neces: To visualize internal organs and structures for potential abnormalities.
rationale.Universal Labs (CBC, CMP, UA): Establishing baseline renal, liver, and electrolyte functions, as well as urinalysis results is essential for a comprehensive workup.
rationale.EKG + CXR if indicated: An EKG can help in detecting cardiac abnormalities while a chest X-ray can aid in identifying lung pathologies.

physical_exam: Routine Check-Up — exam tailored to chief complaint on arrival.
Soft, non-distended, no focal peritoneal signs on initial exam.
Alert and oriented unless perfusion or metabolic derangement present.
No acute rash; capillary refill and perfusion assessed.
order_sets: Imaging studies (X-ray, CT, MRI as necessary)
